titre: The “Nobel Prize” in Economics Is Not a Nobel Prize
accroche: The 1895 will provides for five prizes, none in economics. The one we call that was created in 1968 by Sweden's central bank.
contenu_vulgarise:
Every October, the press announces the “Nobel Prize in economics.” On its own website, however, the Nobel Foundation writes: “The Prize in Economic Sciences is not a Nobel Prize.” Its official name is the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel.

## What the Will Provides

On November 27, 1895, at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel signs his third and last will. In it he earmarks the bulk of his fortune for a fund whose interest will be divided each year into five equal parts: physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature, and a part for whoever has done the most or the best work for fraternity between nations, which will become the peace prize. Economics is not on the list. The reading of the will had already provoked a controversy: his family opposed it, and the institutions he named as juries at first refused the task. It took five years before the first prize, in 1901.

## 1968: A Central Bank Prize

In 1968, the Sveriges Riksbank, Sweden's central bank, makes a donation to the Nobel Foundation on the occasion of its 300th anniversary, and establishes this prize. It has been awarded since 1969 (first laureates: Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen) by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, on the same principles as the Nobel Prizes, for the same amount, paid by the Riksbank. The laureates are announced alongside those of the Nobel Prizes and receive their prize at the same ceremony. Hence the common confusion.

## A Prize Debated Even Among Its Laureates

On December 10, 1974, Friedrich Hayek, co-laureate that year, voices his reservations in his banquet speech: “I must admit that if I had been consulted about whether to create a Nobel Prize in economics, I would have firmly advised against it.” He gives two reasons. The first: such a prize risks, like the activity of certain large scientific foundations, accentuating fashions in science. He judges that the committee brilliantly refuted this fear by crowning views as unfashionable as his own. The second still worries him: the prize confers on an individual an authority that no one in economics should possess. In the natural sciences, he says, an individual's influence is exerted mainly on his peers, who quickly cut him down to size if he exceeds his competence. In economics, the influence that matters is exerted on laymen: policymakers, journalists, civil servants, the public.

Peter Nobel, Alfred's great-grandnephew, maintains for his part that no member of the family ever intended to found an economics prize.

## What the Precision Changes, and What It Doesn't

Saying that it is not a Nobel Prize speaks to its origin and its funding: an 1895 will on one side, a 1968 central bank decision on the other. It says nothing about the seriousness of the selection, entrusted to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. What remains is a question that neither the will nor the Riksbank settles: what authority a prize, whatever its name, gives its recipient among those who cannot verify it.

carte.punch: The “Nobel Prize in economics” is not a Nobel Prize: the Nobel Foundation says so itself.
carte.idee: Alfred Nobel's will (1895) provides for five prizes, none in economics. The economics prize was established in 1968 by the Riksbank. Hayek, co-laureate in 1974, admits in his speech that he would have firmly advised against creating it.

quiz.question: Why does the Nobel Foundation write that the economics prize “is not a Nobel Prize”?
choix: It stems from a 1968 decision by the Swedish central bank, outside the 1895 will
Its selection is entrusted to the Swedish central bank and not to an academy
Alfred Nobel had expressly ruled out economics in his 1895 will
Its amount is lower than that of the five prizes provided for in the will
quiz.explication: The prize was established in 1968 by the Sveriges Riksbank, outside the five prizes of the will. But it is the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences that awards it, for the same amount as the others, and Nobel did not rule out economics: he simply did not mention it.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What exactly does Alfred Nobel's will, signed in 1895, provide for?
choix: Six equal parts, including economics from the start
A single prize, left to the discretion of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
Five equal parts: physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature, and fraternity between nations
Four parts, with economics replacing physiology or medicine
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 1895 will divides the fund into five equal parts: physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature, fraternity between nations, with no mention of economics at all. The other divisions do not appear in the text.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why was the first Nobel Prize not awarded until 1901, six years after the will was signed?
choix: Because Nobel's fortune was not yet available
Because the family opposed it and the designated institutions at first refused the task
Because the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences did not yet exist
Because the Sveriges Riksbank had to validate the rules first
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The article states that the reading of the will provoked a controversy: the family opposed it, and the institutions designated as juries at first refused the task, which delayed the first prize by five years.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What are the two reservations Hayek expresses in 1974 about the existence of an economics prize?
choix: The prize amount, judged too low, and the absence of economics from the 1895 will
Selection by the central bank, and the absence of an independent jury
The lack of international recognition, and competition from other distinctions
The risk of accentuating scientific fashions, and the excessive authority given to an individual among laymen
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Hayek gives two reasons in his speech: such a prize risks accentuating fashions in science, and it confers on an individual an authority that no one in economics should have, since his influence is exerted on laymen and not on peers able to correct him.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does Peter Nobel, Alfred Nobel's great-grandnephew, maintain about the economics prize?
choix: That he personally proposed creating the prize in 1968
That the family approved the prize from its creation
That no member of the family intended to found an economics prize
That he sits today on the committee that awards it
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The article reports that Peter Nobel maintains that no member of the family intended to found an economics prize. The other claims correspond to nothing in the text.
